grateful.oewn-01149996-a.label: positive
grateful.oewn-01149996-a.tone: The plain word for the feeling, with no reservation in it.

thankful.oewn-01149996-a.label: positive
thankful.oewn-01149996-a.tone: Carries a trace of prayer - thanks owed to providence as much as to a person.

appreciative.oewn-01150235-s.label: positive
appreciative.oewn-01150235-s.tone: Cooler and more measured; it values the thing rather than feeling the debt.

glad.oewn-01150423-s.label: positive
glad.oewn-01150423-s.tone: The weakest claim here, and the one most easily said out of politeness.

distrustful.oewn-02472382-a.label: negative
distrustful.oewn-02472382-a.tone: States the position without explaining it - the trust is simply absent.

cynical.oewn-02472810-s.label: negative
cynical.oewn-02472810-s.tone: Assumes the worst motive as a general rule, which saves the trouble of looking.

misanthropic.oewn-02472810-s.label: negative
misanthropic.oewn-02472810-s.tone: The furthest word here: not distrust of a person but of the species.

misanthropical.oewn-02472810-s.label: negative
misanthropical.oewn-02472810-s.tone: The longer form of the same judgement, and rarer.

doubting.oewn-02473075-s.label: neutral
doubting.oewn-02473075-s.tone: Describes a state of mind, and doubt is not a fault in itself.

questioning.oewn-02473075-s.label: neutral
questioning.oewn-02473075-s.tone: Nearly neutral - in most contexts it is what a careful person does.

questioning.oewn-00668084-s.label: neutral
questioning.oewn-00668084-s.tone: The plainest form: the questions are being asked, and nothing is implied about why.

skeptical.oewn-02473075-s.label: neutral
skeptical.oewn-02473075-s.tone: A vice socially and a virtue scientifically; the field decides the charge.

sceptical.oewn-02473075-s.label: neutral
sceptical.oewn-02473075-s.tone: The British spelling, identical in force.

jealous.oewn-02473333-s.label: negative
jealous.oewn-02473333-s.tone: Fear of being displaced. The older sense - jealous of one's honour - was closer to vigilance.

green-eyed.oewn-02473333-s.label: negative
green-eyed.oewn-02473333-s.tone: Shakespeare's monster, and the phrase has outlived the play.

overjealous.oewn-02473333-s.label: negative
overjealous.oewn-02473333-s.tone: Marks the excess explicitly, which suggests some jealousy was warranted.

leery.oewn-02473505-s.label: negative
leery.oewn-02473505-s.tone: Informal and wary rather than hostile; it expects a trick, not a betrayal.

mistrustful.oewn-02473505-s.label: negative
mistrustful.oewn-02473505-s.tone: The plainer twin of *distrustful*, and a shade more tentative.

suspicious.oewn-02473505-s.label: negative
suspicious.oewn-02473505-s.tone: Cuts both ways - a suspicious person and a suspicious package are opposite roles.

untrusting.oewn-02473505-s.label: negative
untrusting.oewn-02473505-s.tone: Built as a plain negative, and it sounds like a diagnosis.

wary.oewn-02473505-s.label: neutral
wary.oewn-02473505-s.tone: Caution that was earned rather than a fault - what experience leaves behind.

eager.oewn-00814485-a.label: positive
eager.oewn-00814485-a.tone: Warm and forward-looking; the desire is presented as a credit to the person.

anxious.oewn-00814817-s.label: neutral
anxious.oewn-00814817-s.tone: This sense means *eagerly desirous* - *anxious to help* - and is easily misread as worry.

dying.oewn-00814817-s.label: neutral
dying.oewn-00814817-s.tone: *Dying to know* - hyperbole worn so smooth the death has gone out of it.

hot.oewn-00814990-s.label: positive
hot.oewn-00814990-s.tone: Enthusiasm at temperature: the wanting is hot rather than steady.

impatient.oewn-00815105-s.label: negative
impatient.oewn-00815105-s.tone: The same energy with the waiting resented - eagerness that has turned on its object.

raring.oewn-00815105-s.label: positive
raring.oewn-00815105-s.tone: *Raring to go* - eagerness with the brakes off.

overeager.oewn-00815276-s.label: negative
overeager.oewn-00815276-s.tone: Names the excess, and implies the eagerness spoiled what it wanted.

curious.oewn-00667636-a.label: positive
curious.oewn-00667636-a.tone: Approving of the mind and faintly wary of the manner - the gloss admits both.

inquisitive.oewn-00668084-s.label: positive
inquisitive.oewn-00668084-s.tone: Praise for a child, and a hint of too many questions for an adult.

speculative.oewn-00668084-s.label: neutral
speculative.oewn-00668084-s.tone: Curiosity aimed at ideas rather than people, and neutral for it.

wondering.oewn-00668084-s.label: positive
wondering.oewn-00668084-s.tone: Curiosity with the wonder still in it, and no agenda attached.

nosy.oewn-00668361-s.label: negative
nosy.oewn-00668361-s.tone: The everyday accusation, and it is about other people's business specifically.

prying.oewn-00668361-s.label: negative
prying.oewn-00668361-s.tone: Names the act rather than the character - the person is doing it right now.

snoopy.oewn-00668361-s.label: negative
snoopy.oewn-00668361-s.tone: Informal and slightly comic, which takes some of the sting out.

overcurious.oewn-00668707-s.label: negative
overcurious.oewn-00668707-s.tone: The formal way of saying nosy, and it grants that curiosity itself was fine.

nonindulgent.oewn-01302836-a.label: neutral
nonindulgent.oewn-01302836-a.tone: A dictionary word rather than a spoken one; it names the absence and stops.

strict.oewn-01302836-a.label: neutral
strict.oewn-01302836-a.tone: Neutral in the balance - a strict teacher is a complaint or a compliment depending on the year.

austere.oewn-01303135-s.label: negative
austere.oewn-01303135-s.tone: Bare rather than harsh, and in architecture and prose it is often praise.

stern.oewn-01303135-s.label: negative
stern.oewn-01303135-s.tone: The face more than the rule; sternness is something the other person can see.

blue.oewn-01303318-s.label: negative
blue.oewn-01303318-s.tone: Strictness of the Sabbath-law kind: moral rigour written into rules.

puritanic.oewn-01303318-s.label: negative
puritanic.oewn-01303318-s.tone: Borrows a whole religious movement to say *no pleasure allowed*.

puritanical.oewn-01303318-s.label: negative
puritanical.oewn-01303318-s.tone: The accusing form - it makes a fault of the strictness rather than a virtue.

corrective.oewn-01303596-s.label: neutral
corrective.oewn-01303596-s.tone: Institutional and euphemistic - it is what discipline is called in a report.

disciplinary.oewn-01303596-s.label: negative
disciplinary.oewn-01303596-s.tone: Used of measures for correcting or punishing misconduct.

disciplinal.oewn-01303596-s.label: negative
disciplinal.oewn-01303596-s.tone: The near-obsolete twin of *disciplinary*: measures meant to correct.

monkish.oewn-01303896-s.label: negative
monkish.oewn-01303896-s.tone: Self-denial by vocation, and slightly mocking when applied outside a monastery.

ill-natured.oewn-01138269-a.label: negative
ill-natured.oewn-01138269-a.tone: Places the fault in the nature, which leaves no room for a bad day.

atrabilious.oewn-01138769-s.label: negative
atrabilious.oewn-01138769-s.tone: Black bile, straight from the four humours; unusable now without irony.

bilious.oewn-01138769-s.label: negative
bilious.oewn-01138769-s.tone: The same medicine, still current, and it makes the temper sound like a symptom.

dyspeptic.oewn-01138769-s.label: negative
dyspeptic.oewn-01138769-s.tone: Sourness of temper with indigestion behind the image - sharp rather than furious.

liverish.oewn-01138769-s.label: negative
liverish.oewn-01138769-s.tone: British and dated - the liver as the seat of a bad mood.

bristly.oewn-01138920-s.label: negative
bristly.oewn-01138920-s.tone: The animal image is doing the work: approach and something goes up.

prickly.oewn-01138920-s.label: negative
prickly.oewn-01138920-s.tone: Touchy about a particular subject rather than in general.

splenetic.oewn-01138920-s.label: negative
splenetic.oewn-01138920-s.tone: Another organ, another temper, and the most literary of the set.

waspish.oewn-01138920-s.label: negative
waspish.oewn-01138920-s.tone: Small, quick and stinging - it describes the remarks more than the mood.

cantankerous.oewn-01139173-s.label: negative
cantankerous.oewn-01139173-s.tone: Difficult by habit rather than by temper; the contrariness is settled, almost fond.

crotchety.oewn-01139173-s.label: negative
crotchety.oewn-01139173-s.tone: Difficulty over small things, and comic rather than frightening.

ornery.oewn-01139173-s.label: negative
ornery.oewn-01139173-s.tone: American and fond as often as not; an ornery mule is being described, not blamed.

choleric.oewn-01139414-s.label: negative
choleric.oewn-01139414-s.tone: The fourth humour. Anger arrives fast and is presented as constitutional.

irascible.oewn-01139414-s.label: negative
irascible.oewn-01139414-s.tone: The formal word for a short fuse, and the most neutral in tone.

hotheaded.oewn-01139414-s.label: negative
hotheaded.oewn-01139414-s.tone: Anger plus poor judgement - the heat is in the thinking.

hot-tempered.oewn-01139414-s.label: negative
hot-tempered.oewn-01139414-s.tone: The plain compound, and the one most likely to be said out loud.

inferior.oewn-02353767-a.label: negative
inferior.oewn-02353767-a.tone: Comparative and cold - it needs something better to exist before it means anything.

bad.oewn-02354208-s.label: negative
bad.oewn-02354208-s.tone: The broadest word in English doing narrow work: below average, and nothing more.

base.oewn-02354354-s.label: negative
base.oewn-02354354-s.tone: Of metals, where it is technical. The moral sense is a separate and much older word.

bum.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
bum.oewn-02354508-s.tone: American and dismissive - *a bum deal*, *a bum knee*.

cheap.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
cheap.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Price used as a verdict on quality, which is the oldest trick in the word.

cheesy.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
cheesy.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Often affectionate about films and pop songs; the badness is part of the appeal.

chintzy.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
chintzy.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Cheapness with a whiff of the shabby-genteel about it.

crummy.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
crummy.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Plain and unliterary, and it complains about the thing rather than sneering at it.

punk.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
punk.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Dated slang for poor quality, long since overtaken by the music.

sleazy.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
sleazy.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Adds moral squalor to shoddiness - the thing is cheap and slightly corrupt.

tinny.oewn-02354508-s.label: negative
tinny.oewn-02354508-s.tone: Specific to sound, and precise enough to be almost neutral.

bush-league.oewn-02354737-s.label: negative
bush-league.oewn-02354737-s.tone: Condescension rather than anger - it rates the thing as small-time and leaves it there.

bush.oewn-02354737-s.label: negative
bush.oewn-02354737-s.tone: The clipped form, and rarer outside American speech.

cheapjack.oewn-02354846-s.label: negative
cheapjack.oewn-02354846-s.tone: Shoddy goods and the hard sell that moves them; it doubts the seller as much as the thing.

shoddy.oewn-02354846-s.label: negative
shoddy.oewn-02354846-s.tone: Poor work passed off as sound - the pretence is as much of the charge as the quality.

tawdry.oewn-02354846-s.label: negative
tawdry.oewn-02354846-s.tone: Cheapness trying to look showy, which is what makes it contemptible rather than merely poor.

noisy.oewn-01926330-a.label: negative
noisy.oewn-01926330-a.tone: The plain complaint, and a mild one - noise is expected in most places.

blatant.oewn-01926766-s.label: negative
blatant.oewn-01926766-s.tone: Bellowing rather than merely loud - the sound is coarse as well as insistent.

clamant.oewn-01926766-s.label: negative
clamant.oewn-01926766-s.tone: Literary and insistent: the noise is a demand rather than a sound.

clamorous.oewn-01926766-s.label: negative
clamorous.oewn-01926766-s.tone: A crowd word - many voices at once, insisting on something.

strident.oewn-01926766-s.label: negative
strident.oewn-01926766-s.tone: Harsh and grating - it condemns the sound of the insisting, not the point insisted on.

vociferous.oewn-01926766-s.label: negative
vociferous.oewn-01926766-s.tone: Loud to the point of offence - the outcry is itself the objection.

abuzz.oewn-01927096-s.label: neutral
abuzz.oewn-01927096-s.tone: Low continuous noise as a sign of life - a room abuzz is a room going well.

buzzing.oewn-01927096-s.label: neutral
buzzing.oewn-01927096-s.tone: The same sound, carrying excitement or irritation with no change of form.

clangorous.oewn-01927233-s.label: negative
clangorous.oewn-01927233-s.tone: Metallic and resonant - a word that makes the sentence loud.

clanging.oewn-01927233-s.label: negative
clanging.oewn-01927233-s.tone: The plain form, and it names the sound without judging it much.

clanking.oewn-01927410-s.label: negative
clanking.oewn-01927410-s.tone: Harder and duller than clanging - chains and machinery rather than bells.

clattery.oewn-01927570-s.label: negative
clattery.oewn-01927570-s.tone: Small hard things in quantity; kitchens and typewriters.

creaky.oewn-01927734-s.label: negative
creaky.oewn-01927734-s.tone: Also used of arguments and institutions, where it means old and barely holding.

creaky.oewn-02591968-s.label: negative
creaky.oewn-02591968-s.tone: The sound stands in for the condition; it suggests one more use might be too many.

screaky.oewn-01927734-s.label: negative
screaky.oewn-01927734-s.tone: The rarer and shriller variant, and it sounds like what it means.

rackety.oewn-01927865-s.label: negative
rackety.oewn-01927865-s.tone: Old-fashioned and slightly fond, as of children.

rip-roaring.oewn-01927865-s.label: neutral
rip-roaring.oewn-01927865-s.tone: Noise as a good time - *a rip-roaring success* has no complaint in it at all.

worn.oewn-02590887-a.label: negative
worn.oewn-02590887-a.tone: Neutral and factual; use leaves marks, and the word says only that.

aged.oewn-02591485-s.label: negative
aged.oewn-02591485-s.tone: The geological sense - a landscape at an advanced stage of erosion.

attrited.oewn-02591610-s.label: negative
attrited.oewn-02591610-s.tone: Technical and rare, from the same root as *attrition*.

battered.oewn-02591692-s.label: negative
battered.oewn-02591692-s.tone: Implies force rather than time, and of a person it means something much worse.

clapped_out.oewn-02591803-s.label: negative
clapped_out.oewn-02591803-s.tone: British, and it works equally on a car, a machine or a person - which is the joke.

decrepit.oewn-02591968-s.label: negative
decrepit.oewn-02591968-s.tone: Broken down past repair, and cruel when turned on a person.

derelict.oewn-02591968-s.label: negative
derelict.oewn-02591968-s.tone: Abandoned as well as ruined - nobody is coming back for it.

flea-bitten.oewn-02591968-s.label: negative
flea-bitten.oewn-02591968-s.tone: Contemptuous and vivid; it adds squalor to mere wear.

run-down.oewn-02591968-s.label: negative
run-down.oewn-02591968-s.tone: Worn by neglect rather than by use; the decline was allowed to happen.

woebegone.oewn-02591968-s.label: negative
woebegone.oewn-02591968-s.tone: Describes the look of sorrow rather than the damage, which makes it oddly gentle.

dog-eared.oewn-02592267-s.label: negative
dog-eared.oewn-02592267-s.tone: The one word here that is nearly affectionate - a dog-eared book was loved.

eared.oewn-02592267-s.label: negative
eared.oewn-02592267-s.tone: The clipped form, and rare enough to be mistaken for the anatomy word.

eroded.oewn-02592502-s.label: negative
eroded.oewn-02592502-s.tone: Geological and neutral; erosion is a process, not a fault.

scoured.oewn-02592502-s.label: negative
scoured.oewn-02592502-s.tone: Worn by water or wind, and the same word means thoroughly cleaned.

frayed.oewn-02592601-s.label: negative
frayed.oewn-02592601-s.tone: Edges only, and forgiving - *frayed nerves* borrows exactly that mildness.
